findings.rule: Incident must fall within the period of cover, and the tier and peril must be covered. COMP covers own damage and collision is a covered event. Superseded v5.3 clauses apply because the incident predates 2026-03-01.
findings.explanation: The incident date of 2026-02-10 falls between inception (2025-11-01) and expiry (2026-10-31). The COMP tier covers own damage. A collision with a guardrail (an object) while driven is a covered event under 2.1. The premium was paid and the incident occurred in Australia. No waiting period clause was supplied, and none was needed to reach this finding. The licence exclusion and the recorded override are outside the cover area and are not assessed here.

findings.rule: A claim must be notified within 30 calendar days of the incident date; later notification needs an explanation (31-90 days) or an approved clause 2.3 exception (beyond 90 days).
findings.calculation: days_incident_to_fnol = 1, which is within the 30-day window, so no late-notification exception is needed.
findings.explanation: The claim was notified 1 day after the incident, well within the 30-day window. Clauses 2.2 and 2.3 are not triggered and no exception was required.

findings.rule: Unlicensed driving is an ABSOLUTE exclusion; an expired licence for any period is treated as no licence and no rebuttal is available. An absolute exclusion may not be overridden at any level, and a recorded override is itself a breach.
findings.explanation: The licence had expired 18 days before the incident, so clause 3.4 treats the driver as unlicensed. Clause 3.4 is ABSOLUTE with no rebuttal available. The licence renewal 9 days after the incident is irrelevant. The claim was accepted and paid (net 5800) with a recorded override of POL-MTR-002:3.4 by L3 with L4 second approval. Clause 4.3 says an absolute exclusion may not be overridden at any level, so the override is invalid and is itself a breach. The decision must be reversed.

findings.rule: Other exclusions (alcohol/drugs, vehicle use, unlisted driver, registration) were checked against the claim facts.
findings.explanation: Vehicle use matches the declared use and registration was current, so neither 3.7 nor 3.15 applies. The driver is the policyholder, so no unlisted driver issue arises. No alcohol or drug exclusion clause was supplied, and no BAC reading was recorded (drug test not tested), so no such exclusion is shown.

findings.rule: Tracks are tested in order; first track whose criteria are met is assigned. Triage within 1 business day. Claim facts: no SIU trigger, not complex, so test fast-track (value <= 5,000, no third party, liability clear, no injury), else Standard.
findings.calculation: Order 1 SIU: score 0 < 60, no indicators, no 5.1 trigger, so not met. Order 2 Complex: value 6,900 <= 50,000, no injury, liability clear, no total loss, so not met. Order 3 Fast-track: estimated value 6,900 > 5,000, so not met (assessed 6,600 also > 5,000). Order 4 Standard: all other claims, so assigned. Triage 1 business day <= 1 allowed.
findings.explanation: The claim was correctly placed on the Standard track because it fails the fast-track value limit of AUD 5,000 and meets no SIU or Complex criteria. Triage happened within 1 business day. No re-triage was needed since the value never crossed a track boundary while on a different track.

findings.rule: Assessment is required for all claims except fast-track claims with sufficient photos; a desktop assessment was done on a STANDARD track claim. The field assessor timeframe applies only where a field assessment is required. No second assessment trigger (written dispute, variance above the greater of 30% or AUD 20,000, or assessor conflict) is present. Quantum is under AUD 100,000. The assessment is not older than 90 days at decision.
findings.calculation: Variance = 6900 - 6600 = 300; 300 / 6900 = 4.3%, below 30%. Threshold is the greater of 30% or AUD 20,000, so not exceeded. Assessment age 3 days is within 90 days. Claim value 6900 is below 100,000.
findings.explanation: An assessment was done (desktop) as required for a standard-track claim. The policy does not require a field assessment here, and the 10 business day allocation and completion timeframes apply only to field assessments. No second assessment trigger applies. The assessment is current at decision, and the quantum is below the independent assessor threshold.

findings.rule: The supplied clauses require dual approval (second approver at Level 3 or above) where a rebuttable exclusion under POL-MTR-002 section 3 is set aside, but they contain no per-level financial limits for settlement. POL-MTR-002 is not supplied, so it cannot be confirmed that exclusion 3.4 is rebuttable and that its rebuttal conditions are met. The L3 limit for a total incurred of 5,800 cannot be checked, and the policy's approval requirement for the set-aside cannot be confirmed.
findings.explanation: Dual approval is recorded (L3 first, L4 second), which meets the 3.1(d) trigger and the Level 3 or above requirement for the second approver if the exclusion is rebuttable. The authority limit table and the text of POL-MTR-002 are not supplied. Whether the first approver's authority covers a 5,800 total incurred, and whether the exclusion is rebuttable or absolute, therefore needs review. If the exclusion is absolute, the override is itself a breach.

findings.rule: POL-AUT-003:3.3 requires both approver identities, roles, levels and timestamps to be recorded. POL-AUT-003:3.2 requires the second approver to be independent of the handler and of the first approver. The claim facts record only levels, so identities, timestamps and reporting lines cannot be checked.
findings.explanation: Only the approver levels are given. Identities, timestamps and whether the L4 approver is the L3 approver's manager or the handler are not in the facts.

findings.rule: Payments must not be split to stay within limits, and there is no denial here. Total incurred equals payments made.
findings.calculation: Payments 5800 = total incurred 5800, with one payment, so no splitting.
findings.explanation: A single payment equals total incurred, so there is no payment splitting. The decision is an acceptance, so denial limits do not apply. The fraud score is 0, so the dual-approval trigger in 3.1(e) does not apply. No late notification exception applies, so 3.1(f) is not triggered.

findings.rule: Fraud score of 0 to 29 is Low band and requires normal handling. No mandatory referral trigger under 5.1 is evidenced, so no SIU referral or block was required.
findings.explanation: No fraud indicators are recorded, so the sum of triggered points is 0 and the recorded score of 0 is correct (Low band). Enhanced verification (30-59) and SIU referral (60+) were not required. Claimed value of 6,900 is far below the 250,000 threshold. No 5.1 trigger is shown in the facts. The licence exception override is outside the fraud area.

findings.rule: Required decision-stage and settlement-stage documents must be on file before the decision (POL-DOC-005 1.3, Appendix A); exception/rebuttal evidence must be on file (3.7).
findings.explanation: Required codes: CLAIM_FORM, ID_VERIFIED, DRIVER_LICENCE (driver in control), PHOTOS, REPAIR_QUOTE_ACCREDITED, ASSESSMENT_REPORT, BANK_VERIFIED (payment), and EXCEPTION_EVIDENCE (rebuttal relied on). All are on file and complete by 2026-02-19, before the 2026-02-20 decision. Claimed amount is under AUD 10,000, so there is no LICENCE_VERIFIED or VEHICLE_HISTORY_CHECK requirement. No third party, injury, police event or GST declaration was needed. The documentation requirement is met; whether the rebuttal itself was valid is outside this area.

findings.rule: Acknowledge within 2 business days of lodgement; decide standard claim within 20 business days of docs-complete; overall cap of 4 months; communicate decision within 5 business days; pay within 10 business days of acceptance; status update at least every 20 business days.
findings.explanation: Acknowledgement 1 bd (limit 2). Standard decision 1 bd from docs complete (limit 20). Decided within 4 months. Communicated in 0 bd (limit 5). Paid 2 bd after acceptance (limit 10). Max contact gap 3 bd (limit 20; claimant not vulnerable). All timeframes met.

findings.rule: Excess is basic excess plus additional excess only if driver under 25, full licence under 2 years, or unlisted driver rebuttal; net = gross minus excess and ITC deduction. No total loss, no recovery.
findings.calculation: Additional excess: driver 52 (not under 25), 34 full licence years (not under 2), driver not unlisted = 0. Expected excess = 800 + 0 = 800. ITC deduction = 0 (not GST registered). Net = 6600 - 800 - 0 = 5800, matches net_paid 5800.
findings.explanation: Excess, ITC, and net settlement are correct. Not a total loss, so the total loss basis does not apply, and no recovery is relevant. The licence exclusion override is outside the settlement area.
